It was King Henry IV of England. He had heard about Owain and the attack on Ruthin. He had heard about the castles Owain and his

In the north of Wales, in a place called Conwy, a very big and strong castle had been captured by the Welsh. It had been built over a hundred years ago by one of the English kings who had first taken over Wales. The Welsh were delighted that it had been captured, they had hated how Conwy Castle reminded them that the English ruled over them. However, the English were angry, how dare the Welsh take it away from them? The English

They were so powerful that they could punch through the armour of a soldier on his horse! God seemed to answer Owain’s prayers as Owain and his soldiers won the battle.

Owain started to think about the chant that he had heard back in his hall in Sycharth. “Owain Glyndwr, Prince of Wales”. He decided that now was the right time to take the
and call himself the Prince of Wales! Ever since the kings of England had started to rule over Wales, they had given the

‘Prince of Wales’ to their oldest son. Now, Owain was saying that he was the Prince of Wales, not the son of the English King! Owain was saying that he was the new ruler of Wales. It seemed as though the Welsh were free again.

Owain was afraid. Not only had his

failed, but the rest of his family was not safe. The English had taken them prisoner! Owain would never get to see them again... To escape the English, he wandered alone across Wales disguised as a shepherd. However, he was not done fighting, after all, he was the Prince of Wales! Now and again, Owain would gather together a small group of soldiers and ambush English soldiers.

Eventually though, Owain’s attacks stopped. Historians do not know exactly where he went or what happened to him. Some people say that in his journeys across Wales he came across the ruins of his old house at Sycharth. Upset by what he saw, he chose to end his
against the English and live a life without fighting.
